rationale: The promise diagnostics settle the upstream question and refute the leading explanation. In convergence round 3 node 4 received four Promises carrying its ballot n=2: nodes 1, 2 and 5 each reported accept round 1, accepted index 37 and a log_sync containing the StopSign, while node 3 reported accept round 0 and accepted index 0 with no StopSign. The greatest PromiseMetaData is one of the StopSign-bearing promises, so the single max_promise_sync merge delivered the StopSign, and node 4's own accepted index rose from 0 to 37 in that same round. The max-merge hazard therefore did not drop the StopSign here; what the receipt does show is that node 4 acquired the StopSign in round 3, after it had already sent node 3 the AcceptSync that brought node 3 to accepted 37. This update records that evidence, refutes the max-merge attribution for run 13 and restates the interpretation around the timing that remains open.

knowledge.statement: In convergence round 3 of the seeded run 13, the four Promises delivered to node 4 carried ballot n=2 and read: from1 na1 aidx37 didx0 ss1, from2 na1 aidx37 didx0 ss1, from3 na0 aidx0 didx0 ss0, from5 na1 aidx37 didx0 ss1. Node 4's accepted index changed from 0 to 37 in that same round and stayed 37, while its decided index ended at 38. No Promise addressed to node 4 was delivered during the earlier 900 randomized actions.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 with 20 percent out-of-order loss, then 150 fair-delivery rounds; Promises are recorded only when actually delivered to pid 4 and only the first forty are kept, and node 4's accepted index is sampled after each convergence round.

knowledge.assertion: Refutes the max-merge attribution for run 13: three StopSign-bearing Promises with the greatest meta were delivered to node 4 and its accepted index rose 0 -> 37 in the same round, so the single max promise merge did deliver the StopSign.
Still a real ordering hazard in general, but not the cause of run 13: the delivered StopSign-bearing promises outranked the empty one, so the merge did not drop the StopSign there.
Not needed for run 13 either: the StopSign reached leader 4 through a Promise that was part of the recorded round-3 set, so a late unmerged Promise is not the observed path.
Applies: node 4 ended with accepted 37 and decided 38, so its decided index exceeded its own accepted index and must have been set from follower-reported accepted indices.

interpretations.rationale: The executed receipts show the stall, its mechanism and what the leader knew when. Receipt 603b748c50264e55a054c67805af4fab reran randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag (exit 0, test passed) with the promise diagnostics; its comparison (converged_all true, gated on progressed and reconfigured) is complete and violated on event 1, which again reports decided 38,38,37,38,38 after 150 fair-delivery rounds and node 3 at accepted 37, decided 37, leader pid 4, promise ballot n=2, zero PrepareReq, with node 3's inbound trace prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|accsync1:0-0>37-0|decide2:37-0>37-37|decide3:37-37>37-37. The same event records that node 4 received four Promises for ballot n=2 in convergence round 3: nodes 1, 2 and 5 each reported accept round 1, accepted index 37 and a log_sync containing the StopSign, while node 3 reported accept round 0 and accepted 0 without a StopSign. Because PromiseMetaData orders by accept round first and accepted index second, the greatest promise is one of the StopSign-bearing ones, so the single log_sync merged at the prepare quorum did carry the StopSign, and node 4's accepted index rose 0 -> 37 in that same round. The max-merge hazard is therefore not the cause of this run: leader 4 did acquire the StopSign, but only in round 3, after it had already sent node 3 the AcceptSync that left node 3 at accepted 37 with decided 0. The two later Decides carry counters 2 and 3, the immediate successors of that AcceptSync, so check_msg_status treats them as expected and handle_decide clamps decided to the flushed accepted index: the first moves decided 0 -> 37, the second leaves 37. Node 3 never sends a PrepareReq, so no reconnection and no further AcceptSync follow, and no AcceptStopSign reaches node 3 at any point in the window. Node 4 meanwhile ends with accepted 37 but decided 38, which is only possible because is_chosen counted follower-reported accepted indices. What remains open is the exact position node 3 lacks: the promises show the StopSign holders at accepted 37, the same accepted index node 3 reached from its AcceptSync, so the receipt cannot say whether node 3's position 37 is the StopSign or whether the decision at 38 references a position the leader never carried in its own log. The progress loss itself is established: a decided index node 3 cannot accept, a sequence-expected Decide path that clamps instead of repairing, and no recovery across 150 fair-delivery rounds. Agreement is unaffected because no two nodes reported different values at any decided index.
counterevidence: A missing AcceptStopSign does not always stall: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead and the follower reconnected, after which an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, so those events give the follower a fresh sequence and a new log sync.
Agreement is unaffected: divergences stayed 0 and no node reported a different value at a decided index, so this is a progress/availability defect for one follower.
The max-merge explanation is refuted for this run: the StopSign-bearing promises were the greatest and the leader's accepted index rose 0 -> 37, so the StopSign was not dropped by the merge.
limitations: One seeded schedule and one lagging follower; node 3's inbound trace is capped at twelve messages after the lossy phase, and Promises to node 4 are recorded only when delivered and only up to forty entries.

Because the promise diagnostics sample node 4 only once per round and the AcceptSync to node 3 was emitted earlier in the same or an earlier round, the receipt orders the sync before the merge but does not pin the acceptance moment more precisely.
The receipt does not record the log_sync content of node 3's AcceptSync or the value at the missing position, so whether node 3 lacks the StopSign itself or a later position is unresolved.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
